literature_notes: All four ledger lines (L1–L4) describe a single C-terminal FLAG-tagged DLL3 construct expressed in mammalian cells (SCLC lines, CHO). DLL3 is a type I single-pass transmembrane protein: the extracellular domain spans residues 27–491, the TM helix 492–513, and the cytoplasmic tail 514–618. L1 explicitly states 'C-terminal FLAG tag'; L4 confirms this with a domain schematic ordered Signal → DSL → EGF1–6 → TM → F, placing the FLAG after the TM domain and therefore in the intracellular tail. L2 and L3 validate the same construct functionally (cis-inhibition of Notch; co-IP with LFNG) but add no new positional information. No ledger line reports a tag insertion on the extracellular face of full-length, membrane-anchored DLL3. Zero surface tag sites are supported.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal FLAG tag appended after the last residue (K618); the DLL3 C-terminus lies in the intracellular tail (residues 514–618), so this tag faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular space. Functional: construct suppresses Notch signaling in cis (L2) and co-IPs with LFNG (L3).
